blocks.text: Fire hydrant system

A fire hydrant system supplies pressurized water to fire hoses and hose reels positioned around a building or site, giving firefighting teams direct access to water during an emergency. Firestone Fire and Security Systems designs, installs, and maintains fire hydrant systems for commercial, industrial, and residential properties across the UAE, in full compliance with civil defence requirements.
Get a quote
Why you need a fire hydrant system

A fire hydrant system gives firefighting teams an immediate, on-site water source instead of relying on tankers or the nearest public hydrant, which can add critical minutes to a response during a fire. For larger properties, that time difference often determines whether a fire stays contained or spreads before help arrives.Beyond emergency response, a fire hydrant system is frequently a civil defence approval requirement rather than an optional upgrade. Buildings above a certain footprint, height, or occupancy are assessed during the design and licensing stage, and a missing or non-compliant hydrant system can hold up a building's completion certificate, Istifa, or ongoing occupancy approval.A properly designed system also protects the value of the property itself. Insurers and facility managers factor fire protection infrastructure into risk assessments, and a documented, tested hydrant system can support better terms and demonstrate that the building meets its ongoing safety obligations, not just its initial approval.
Our fire hydrant services
Firestone provides end-to-end fire hydrant system support, from initial design through to ongoing compliance.

Coverage across the UAE
Service delivery in Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Sharjah, and Al Ain, under ADCD, DCD, and SCD requirements.
Choose the right system for you building
Warehouses and industrial facilities
Large open footprints usually need an external hydrant ring main with multiple outlets spaced around the perimeter, giving firefighters access from any side of the building.
Labor accommodation and residential compounds
Multi-building sites benefit from a shared hydrant network connecting several blocks to a single water source, reducing the number of separate systems required across the compound.
High-rise and mid-rise buildings
Taller buildings are usually required to pair an external hydrant system with an internal wet riser, since ground-level hydrants alone cannot serve upper floors effectively.
Construction sites
Temporary hydrant systems are often required during the build phase itself, ahead of the permanent fire protection installation, to meet civil defence site safety requirements.
Mixed-use and commercial plots

Sites with several buildings or varied occupancy types typically need a hydrant layout designed around the highest-risk building on the plot, with spacing and flow rates calculated to cover the whole site.

A site survey is the only reliable way to confirm which configuration applies, since civil defence authorities assess spacing, flow rate, and pump sizing against the specific building rather than a fixed template.

blocks.text: What Happens During a Civil Defence Inspection
A civil defence inspection reviews whether a fire hydrant system remains fully functional and compliant since its last approval. Inspectors typically check:

items: Hydrant outlets are accessible and unobstructed
Pressure and flow meet the levels set during design
Pipework shows no signs of corrosion or leakage
Maintenance records and previous test reports are reviewed
